**AIA Group Limited** ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): 友邦保險) is a Hong Kong [multinational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation") [insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurance "Insurance") and finance company. It is one of the largest publicly traded [life insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_insurance "Life insurance") groups in the [Asia-Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia-Pacific "Asia-Pacific"). AIA traces back to an American insurance firm that was established in [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai"), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") in 1919. The company then became the founding member of the [American International Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group "American International Group") (AIG) conglomerate, from which it was separated after the [2008 global financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_global_financial_crisis "2008 global financial crisis").

AIA underwrites life insurance for individuals and businesses, as well as accident and health insurance. It provides retirement planning and wealth management services, variable contracts, investments and securities. It and its wholly-owned subsidiaries operate in 18 markets in East Asia and Oceania, with more than 43 million policyholders.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=AIA_Group&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

See also: [American International Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group "American International Group")

### Precursor companies in Shanghai

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=AIA_Group&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Precursor companies in Shanghai")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/Shanghai_of_Today%2C_Plate_9_-_North_China_Daily_News_building.jpg/250px-Shanghai_of_Today%2C_Plate_9_-_North_China_Daily_News_building.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shanghai_of_Today,_Plate_9_-_North_China_Daily_News_building.jpg)

American Asiatic Underwriters operated from the [North China Daily News Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_China_Daily_News_Building "North China Daily News Building") (left) on [The Bund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bund "The Bund") from 1927 before vacating due to [Japan's occupation of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_occupation_of_Shanghai "Japanese occupation of Shanghai").[[4]](#cite_note-ji2016-4): 157 The Shanghai branch of AIA returned to the building in 1996.

American businessman [Cornelius Vander Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelius_Vander_Starr "Cornelius Vander Starr") worked in the vehicle insurance business in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") before joining the [US Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Army "US Army") during [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") and then working in the steamship business in [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan"). He then moved to Shanghai, where he was employed by American banking tycoon Frank Jay Raven to manage his insurance agency.[[5]](#cite_note-fallengiant-5): 20–21

On 19 December 1919, Starr founded his own small insurance company called American Asiatic Underwriters in Shanghai that specialized in products covering fire and marine risks.[[6]](#cite_note-enrich-6)[[7]](#cite_note-7): 79 It operated as an agent for other American insurers,[[6]](#cite_note-enrich-6): 119–120 each assuming a portion of the risk insured by Starr's business without the need to deploy employees abroad.[[8]](#cite_note-8): 7

Using funds from American Asiatic Underwriters, Starr founded Asia Life Insurance two years later. The new company became the first foreign company to sell life insurances to local Chinese customers.[[6]](#cite_note-enrich-6): 120 Both moved into [17 The Bund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_China_Daily_News_Building "North China Daily News Building") in 1927, after Starr purchased the building as a center for banking and insurance.

### Founding

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=AIA_Group&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Founding")]

In April 1931, Starr established International Assurance Company in Shanghai, with British and Chinese partners. In 1933, AIA opened a branch in [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore") that also served [Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Malaya "British Malaya").[[9]](#cite_note-lee2012-9): 397

American Asiatic Underwriters and Asia Life Insurance collectively gained control over 30% of the Chinese insurance industry, and by 1937, 75% of China's insurance income, valued at 38.8 million [fabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_National_Currency "Chinese National Currency"), could be attributed to the latter.[[4]](#cite_note-ji2016-4): 157

In 1939, the American Asiatic Underwriters headquarters was relocated to [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") after the [Japanese invasion of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Shanghai "Battle of Shanghai") and the Japanese military forced the business to stop in 1941.[[10]](#cite_note-sun2007-10): 599 After the end of the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), AIA was the first foreign insurance company to resume operations.[[11]](#cite_note-chan2012-11): 21

On 1 January 1949, K.K. Tse moved American Asiatic Underwriters's regional headquarters, 40 employees and their families, and company records to Hong Kong.[[5]](#cite_note-fallengiant-5): 60 Before the company's closure in December 1950,[[5]](#cite_note-fallengiant-5): 60–62

### Relocation to Hong Kong

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=AIA_Group&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Relocation to Hong Kong")]

After the [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_China "Communist Party of China") takeover of mainland China, AIA's headquarters were relocated again, to the British colony of [Hong Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong").[[11]](#cite_note-chan2012-11): 82 In 1970, AIA became a subsidiary of New York-based [American International Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group "American International Group") (AIG), which was formed as a holding company for Starr's companies in the US.[[11]](#cite_note-chan2012-11): 82 In June 1951, Starr's companies stopped operations in Shanghai.[[10]](#cite_note-sun2007-10)

Despite AIG not operating in China, it maintained close ties with the Chinese leadership. Between 1975 and 1992, its CEO and chairman [Maurice R. Greenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_R._Greenberg "Maurice R. Greenberg") traveled to China dozens of times to fraternise with officials including [Jiang Zemin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiang_Zemin "Jiang Zemin") and [Zhu Rongji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhu_Rongji "Zhu Rongji") when they were the [mayor of Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Shanghai "Mayor of Shanghai"). Jiang and Zhu later respectively became China's president and premier. Greenberg also sat in an advisory board to the mayor, while the company helped draft China's 1995 insurance law, persuade the [US Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") to support China's ascension to the [World Trade Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization"), and establish a New York branch of the [Chinese central bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Bank_of_China "People's Bank of China").[[12]](#cite_note-12)

### Return to China

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=AIA_Group&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Return to China")]

The Chinese government gradually removed restrictions on foreign businesses after its [reform and opening up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_and_opening_up "Reform and opening up") that began in 1979. On 25 September 1992, AIA became one of the first companies to be granted the foreign insurer licenses to operate in China.[[11]](#cite_note-chan2012-11): 3 The companies marketed the event as a "return home".[[11]](#cite_note-chan2012-11): 81–83 AIA's top managers came from Hong Kong and Taiwan, while low- and mid-level managers were mainland Chinese, most being local employees from Shanghai.[[11]](#cite_note-chan2012-11): 85

### Financial crisis and listing

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=AIA_Group&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Financial crisis and listing")]

During the [US subprime mortgage crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subprime_mortgage_crisis "Subprime mortgage crisis") of 2007, AIG nearly went bankrupt because it assumed outsized risk on bets on the property market that resulted in losses worth billions of dollars. It was rescued by the [US Treasury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury "United States Department of the Treasury"), the [Federal Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve "Federal Reserve"), and the [Federal Reserve Bank of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_New_York "Federal Reserve Bank of New York") through various means, including the creation of [special-purpose vehicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_purpose_vehicles "Special purpose vehicles").[[13]](#cite_note-13)

On 1 December 2009, AIG sold preferred equity interests in two newly formed international life insurance subsidiaries, American International Assurance Company, Limited (AIA) and [American Life Insurance Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Life_Insurance_Company "American Life Insurance Company") (ALICO), to the [Federal Reserve Bank of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_New_York "Federal Reserve Bank of New York") to reduce its debt by US$25 billion.[[1]](#cite_note-AIGAIA-1)

By 2009, AIG had planned to list AIA on the [Hong Kong Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_Stock_Exchange "Hong Kong Stock Exchange") with [The Blackstone Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blackstone_Group "The Blackstone Group") hired as an IPO advisor.[[14]](#cite_note-14) The [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") was intended to help AIG repay US$182.3 billion bailout credit line from the US government.[[15]](#cite_note-businessweek-15) Before the planned listing, [Prudential plc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_plc "Prudential plc"), the UK's largest insurance firm, offered to buy AIA for US$35.5 billion to expand its Asian business as growth in the UK declined.[[15]](#cite_note-businessweek-15)[[16]](#cite_note-16) Prudential shareholders voted against the purchase price, which was then reduced to US$30.4 billion. AIG rejected the smaller offer, and the attempted acquisition failed.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

AIA held an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") on 29 October 2010 that raised approximately HK$159.08 billion (US$20.51 billion), making it the third largest IPO in history.[[18]](#cite_note-18) The IPO price was set at a lower valuation than its public competitors in Asia-Pacific. Shares rose 17% with two billion shares changing hands on the first trading day.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

The stake of AIA Aurora (controlled by AIG) was diluted to 32.9%. At one point, AIA was tied with [Tencent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tencent "Tencent") as the largest constituent of the Hang Seng Index during the February 2021 review.[[20]](#cite_note-20) However, following multiple index adjustments, its weighting declined to 4.72% as of June 2025.[[21]](#cite_note-21)

On 11 September 2012, AIA acquired a 92.3% stake in Sri Lankan insurer Aviva NDB Insurance from British insurer [Aviva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviva "Aviva") and Sri Lanka's [NDB Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NDB_Bank "NDB Bank"), one of Sri Lanka's largest financial conglomerates. AIA also entered into an exclusive 20-year [bancassurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bancassurance "Bancassurance") agreement with NDB. On 7 October, AIA acquired [ING Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ING_Group "ING Group")'s Malaysian insurance subsidiaries for a cash consideration of €1.336 billion (US$1.73 billion).[[22]](#cite_note-22) On 21 December, AIG sold all of its 13.69% shareholding in AIA.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

Since 2 June 2013, AIA has had an exclusive [bancassurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bancassurance "Bancassurance") agreement with [Citibank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citibank "Citibank") that encompasses 11 AIA markets in Asia-Pacific, namely Hong Kong, mainland China, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Australia, and India.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

In August 2024, the Hong Kong [Insurance Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurance_Authority "Insurance Authority") fined AIA HK$23 million for shortcomings related to its anti-money laundering (AML) oversight.[[25]](#cite_note-25) The inspection, which covered business activities between March 2016 and October 2022, identified deficiencies in the company's anti-money laundering systems, including delays in identifying certain politically exposed persons and in applying enhanced due diligence to some high-risk customers.[[26]](#cite_note-26)

args.summary:
AIA Group Limited is a Hong Kong-based multinational insurance and finance company, one of the largest publicly traded life insurance groups in the Asia-Pacific region. It was founded on December 19, 1919, in Shanghai by American businessman Cornelius Vander Starr as American Asiatic Underwriters, and later became the founding member of American International Group (AIG). After the 2008 global financial crisis, AIA was separated from AIG.

Key historical milestones:
- 1919: Founded in Shanghai as American Asiatic Underwriters
- 1931: Starr established International Assurance Company in Shanghai
- 1949-1950: Moved headquarters to Hong Kong following the communist takeover of mainland China
- 1970: Became a subsidiary of AIG
- 1992: Became one of the first foreign insurers granted licenses to operate in China
- 2010: Held an IPO on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, raising approximately HK$159.08 billion (US$20.51 billion), making it the third largest IPO in history at the time
- 2012: AIG sold its remaining stake in AIA; AIA acquired ING's Malaysian insurance subsidiaries and Aviva NDB Insurance in Sri Lanka
- 2013: Entered exclusive bancassurance agreement with Citibank in 11 Asia-Pacific markets
- 2024: Fined HK$23 million by Hong Kong Insurance Authority for anti-money laundering compliance deficiencies

AIA underwrites life insurance, accident and health insurance, and provides retirement planning and wealth management services. It operates in 18 markets across East Asia and Oceania with more than 43 million policyholders. As of 2025, the company reported net income of US$6.27 billion, total assets of US$345 billion, and total equity of US$48 billion. Its current president and CEO is Lee Yuan Siong.

# AIA

**AIA: Everything you need to know**

| Key people | Lee Yuan Siong (group chief executive and president) |

**History**

AIA Group was founded on June 02, 1919, and is the largest pan-Asian life insurance group offering insurance and financial services products.

AIA is based in Hong Kong, and currently has a presence across 18 markets in the Asia-Pacific region. It was founded in Shanghai as American Asiatic Underwriters before relocating its business to New York City in 1939, where it became a subsidiary of American International Group (AIG).

AIA planned to be listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2010, however, was set to be purchased by Prudential Plc for US$35.5 billion on March 02, 2010. When the purchase fell through, AIA held an IPO which raised roughly HK$20.51 billion, the third largest IPO globally to this day. The group has an exclusive bancassurance agreement with Citibank that covers 11 Asia-Pacific AIA markets including Hong Kong, India, Thailand, Singapore and Australia.

**New Zealand**

AIA commenced its New Zealand operations in 1981 as a member of the American Life Insurance Company (ALICO) and is headquartered in Takapuna, Auckland.

In 2017, AIA reached an agreement with the Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) to acquire its Australian life insurance business, along with its life and health insurance businesses in New Zealand. It also entered into a 20-year strategic bancassurance partnership with CBA in both Australia and New Zealand, a transaction which provided access to the bank’s 12 million existing customers and was expected to “deliver a range of important benefits to AIA and its stakeholders,” securing its place as a leading life insurer in the New Zealand market.

According to AIA, its purpose in New Zealand is to provide “simple yet innovative insurance solutions that suit the Kiwi way of life,” and it works through an “extensive network of insurance advisers and organisations.”

In 2018, AIA announced its acquisition of Sovereign, one of New Zealand’s largest life and health insurers. Sovereign now operates under the AIA brand, with the latter being transformed into New Zealand’s largest life insurer.

Commenting on the acquisition, AIA head of Australia and New Zealand Damien Mu said: “This puts us in a unique position to address the nation’s significant insurance gap. AIA is committed to helping make New Zealand one of the healthiest and most protected nations in the world – we will do this as a customer-centric organisation that delivers valued insurance propositions to our customers. These include AIA Vitality, which will be launched in New Zealand in the near future, and AIA’s established rehabilitation and return to work programmes, both of which are helping people live healthier, longer, better lives.”

**Products**

AIA’s New Zealand branch offers a range of life, health and income protection cover geared towards both individuals and businesses. Its key product offerings are the following.

* *Life cover*: AIA offers a vast range of life insurance policies. Its product suite includes real trauma cover for those seriously affected by a major illness, and cover for accidental death and total and permanent disability cover (TPD), which provides a lump sum payment of up to $5,000,000 if you are disabled and unlikely to work again. AIA’s trauma cover also offers an optional cancer treatment benefit add-on, which assists with the cost of specialist consultations and tests for the diagnosis of cancer.
* *Health*: AIA’s REAL Health cover offers hospital, surgical and diagnostic benefits among others, and is designed to help deal with the mounting costs of New Zealand’s private medical healthcare.
* *Income protection*: This suite of products offers financial assistance in the event of an accident or injury, and can cover mortgage payments, rent and other living costs. This is usually paid out as a monthly benefit, and can cover either a part of, or the full amount, of any costs.
* *Business life and income*: AIA’s business life cover provides a one-off payment in the event of a death to ensure business continuity. Business income protection, which includes a policy tailored for the farming industry, offers cover for business income if a key person is incapacitated.

**Leadership**

**Lee Yuan Siong - executive director, group chief executive and president**

Lee was appointed executive director and the group chief executive and president on 1 June 2020. He is also a member of the AIA’s risk committee. He joined the group in March 2020.

Lee has more than 30 years of experience in the insurance sector. He has served as a director of various companies within the group, including as acting chairman and chief executive officer of AIA Company Limited.

Prior to his current role, Lee was an executive director of Ping An Insurance (Group) Company of China, Ltd. from June 2013 and served as the company’s co-CEO and chief insurance Business Officer. Before joining Ping An, he held several senior leadership positions with Prudential plc of the United Kingdom, including president of CITIC-Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited, a life insurance joint venture in Mainland China. He also has significant experience across various Asian markets, including Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Taiwan (China), Thailand, and Vietnam.

**Charitable activity**

AIA is involved in New Zealand’s Healthiest Schools Challenge along with Sovereign – a six-week programme promoting fitness and health across 500 primary and intermediate schools across the country. Each registered supporter gives their chosen school a chance to win $50,000 in sports grants.

The initiative was previously run as the AIA Healthy Kids Challenge in 2016.

No todo pasa por la suba del costo: los dilemas que atraviesa la construcción y los desafíos para la industria hacia 2030 A partir del análisis de 31 especialistas internacionales se pueden identificar cinco cambios que impulsarán la transformación del sector de la construcción durante los próximos años 15 de agosto de 2026 07:07 Agregar LA NACION en En Argentina, la construcción atraviesa una de sus crisis más complejas y delicadas de los últimos añosFotomontaje realizado con IA Agregar en En la Argentina, la construcción atraviesa una de sus crisis más complejas y delicadas de los últimos años, con un costo que sigue subiendo y una importante caída de la obra pública que impactan en la actividad de manera directa. Es más, la construcción fue el sector con peor desempeño entre el cuarto trimestre de 2023 y el tercero de 2025, registrando una caída acumulada del 11%, mientras que el PBI total creció casi un 2% en el mismo periodo. La fuerte reducción en las obras financiadas por el Estado impactó negativamente, dejando a la inversión privada como el único motor, aunque esta todavía tiene un impulso limitado. A eso se suma otro frente sensible: los costos . Si bien en los últimos meses el ritmo de aumento se desaceleró, todavía siguen corriendo por encima de los aumentos del valor de venta de las propiedades, lo que comprime considerablemente los márgenes de rentabilidad de los desarrolladores. Un ejemplo: en junio de 2026, el nivel general del índice del costo de la construcción (ICC) en el Gran Buenos Aires registró una suba del 2,6% respecto al mes anterior y del 32,1% a nivel interanual; mientras que el precio medio de un departamento subió 0,2% en el mismo período, de acuerdo con los datos de Zonaprop. Los costos de construcción todavía siguen corriendo por encima del valor de venta de las propiedadesShutterstock Pero el desafío de la construcción no es solo argentino. Un informe global advierte que los riesgos que enfrentará la industria de la construcción en los próximos cinco años ya no funcionan como problemas aislados, sino como una cadena: la escasez de talento acelera la automatización; la automatización permite comprimir plazos; los plazos más ajustados reducen la tolerancia ante interrupciones; el clima extremo desafía los supuestos de diseño; y el capital penaliza cada vez más los retrasos. En otras palabras, el mundo quiere construir más, más rápido y con mayor complejidad, pero la mano de obra, el financiamiento, los seguros, la tecnología y los sistemas de apoyo no siempre acompañan ese ritmo. Una obra parada ya no es solo una construcción que se detuvo, sino que puede transformarse en un problema financiero, operativo y asegurador al mismo tiempo. Ese es el punto central de Beyond 2030: The Future of Construction , un informe global de Zurich Insurance Group elaborado a partir del análisis de 31 especialistas internacionales en suscripción, siniestros, ingeniería de riesgos y construcción. “Nuestros clientes están desarrollando proyectos cada vez más complejos en un entorno de riesgos más volátil, además de plazos más ajustados. Nuestra investigación más reciente deja claro que, si un proyecto no es asegurable, no será financiado. Por ello, incorporar resiliencia desde el diseño, con las aseguradoras participando desde etapas tempranas, es clave para que los proyectos sean viables”, señaló Kelly Kinzer, Global Head of Construction & Surety de Zurich Insurance Group. En ese marco, el informe identifica cinco cambios que impulsarán la transformación de la industria durante los próximos cinco años. 1) El clima deja de ser una variable externa El informe ubica a los eventos climáticos extremos y los desastres naturales como el principal riesgo para el sector, con una calificación de 6,2 puntos sobre 7. El cambio climático impone la necesidad de repensar la resiliencia de las obras desde su diseño. Si un proyecto no contempla la adaptación a estas nuevas condiciones del entorno, enfrentará severas interrupciones físicas. En proyectos de alta demanda energética, como los centros de datos, el riesgo se vuelve todavía más tangible. Zurich advierte que el calor extremo y las sequías amenazan directamente los sistemas de refrigeración por agua y el suministro eléctrico, transformando el riesgo climático en un peligro de paralización operativa inmediata que compromete la seguridad de la infraestructura. 2) Un mercado de capitales cada vez más exigente El segundo desafío tiene que ver con que el acceso al financiamiento sigue disponible para proyectos estratégicos, pero los inversores muestran una tolerancia cada vez menor a los retrasos, sobrecostos y problemas de ejecución. Con un nivel de riesgo de 5,7 sobre 7, la expansión de modelos de financiamiento más sofisticados está trasladando los riesgos de construcción hacia etapas cada vez más tempranas del ciclo de vida de los proyectos. En este contexto, aspectos como la ubicación, la disponibilidad de recursos, la capacidad de ejecución y la asegurabilidad adquieren un peso creciente en las decisiones de inversión. La expansión de modelos de financiamiento más sofisticados está trasladando los riesgos de construcción hacia etapas cada vez más tempranas del ciclo de vida de los proyectosDaniel Basualdo Ese cambio pega de lleno en América Latina, donde la competencia por capital para infraestructura energética, logística, tecnológica y sanitaria se intensifica. En la Argentina, el caso más evidente está en Vaca Muerta, donde proyectos como el oleoducto Vaca Muerta Oil Sur (VMOS) y las obras de ampliación de infraestructura de transporte energético requieren importantes inversiones y una ejecución eficiente para asegurar su viabilidad económica. 3) Falta talento, pero también falta experiencia crítica El tercer desafío global es la escasez de talento especializado y la pérdida de conocimiento crítico, con una calificación de 5,6 sobre 7. La construcción atraviesa una transformación profunda donde el desafío ya no es solo incorporar más trabajadores, sino contar con perfiles técnicos capaces de gestionar proyectos cada vez más digitalizados y complejos. En la Argentina, el escenario ya es complejo: según ManpowerGroup, el 68% de las empresas reporta dificultades para encontrar los perfiles técnicos y profesionales que necesita. Un informe confirma que se siguen perdiendo puestos de trabajo en la industria de la construcciónImagen ilustrativa generada con IA A este panorama se suma un riesgo menos visible: el retiro de los trabajadores experimentados. A medida que avanzan la automatización y la industrialización, la experiencia acumulada para supervisar sistemas complejos, coordinar disciplinas y resolver problemas operativos en el terreno se vuelve un recurso tan escaso y valioso como la propia mano de obra. Los datos locales muestran una recuperación parcial del empleo formal, aunque todavía con fragilidades. El Ieric (Instituto de Estadística y Registro de la Industria de la Construcción) informó que en abril de 2026 el empleo registrado en la industria de la construcción llegó a 357.679 puestos, nivel que representa una baja del 1,4% mensual, equivalente a una reducción de 4903. En mayo tuvo una caída del 0,8% con 355.962 puestos de trabajo; con una nueva baja estimada en 0,4% para los datos sobre junio. El nivel actual todavía se ubica entre un 10% y 11% por debajo de la media histórica de esos meses, calculada sin incluir los años de pandemia. 4) La adopción de la construcción modular y la prefabricación Para compensar la falta de personal calificado y acortar plazos, la industria acelera la adopción de construcción modular y prefabricación, un riesgo que Zurich califica con 5,1 puntos sobre 7. El informe señala que la adopción de estos métodos pasó del 32% al 50% en el último año. En la Argentina, donde los costos de construcción y los plazos son dos obsesiones permanentes para desarrolladores y compradores, la idea de construir más rápido tiene un plus adicional. El modelo “llave en mano”, las casas industrializadas, el steel frame, los paneles premoldeados y los sistemas modulares empiezan a ganar lugar porque prometen reducir la exposición a la inflación de costos durante períodos largos. Sin embargo, esta automatización introduce un riesgo nuevo: la réplica de diseños y sistemas complejos a gran escala antes de conocer del todo su comportamiento a largo plazo. El ejemplo más claro de esta complejidad técnica y de concentración de riesgo son los centros de datos. Por eso, hacia 2030, la clave no será solo construir más rápido, sino demostrar que esa velocidad no compromete durabilidad, seguridad ni asegurabilidad. En la Argentina, los costos de construcción y los plazos son dos obsesiones permanentes para desarrolladores y compradoresRicardo Pristupluk 5) La digitalización de la construcción y amenazas cibernéticas El quinto desafío, con un nivel de riesgo de 4,8 puntos sobre 7, tiene que ver con la introducción de los procesos de digitalización en la construcción y cómo están transformando la manera de diseñar, coordinar y operar proyectos, pero también amplían la superficie de exposición a incidentes cibernéticos. Actualmente, cuatro de cada cinco empresas de arquitectura, ingeniería y construcción reportaron haber sufrido amenazas de ciberseguridad durante los últimos dos años, con un promedio de 226 incidentes anuales por compañía. “La construcción cumple un rol fundamental en la economía argentina por su capacidad de dinamizar la inversión y generar desarrollo. Sin embargo, los proyectos actuales enfrentan un entorno de riesgos cada vez más complejo, con mayores exigencias en materia de financiamiento, ejecución y resiliencia. Hoy, incorporar una visión integral del riesgo desde el diseño ya no es un diferencial, sino una condición necesaria para que los proyectos sean viables, financiables y sostenibles en el largo plazo”, afirmó Alejandro Vega Cigoj, Head of Commercial Insurance de Zurich Argentina. Para el mercado argentino, los desafíos hacia 2030 no se resumen en una sola variable. No es solo la inflación de costos, ni solo la falta de crédito, ni solo la caída de la obra pública, ni solo la escasez de talento. Es la combinación de todos esos impactos al mismo tiempo.

**Zurich Insurance Group Ltd.** is a Swiss [insurance company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurance_company "Insurance company"), headquartered in [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zürich "Zürich"), and the country's largest insurer.[[2]](#cite_note-2) As of 2024,[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit) the group is the world's 98th largest public company according to *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")*' Global 2000s list,[[3]](#cite_note-3) and in 2011, it ranked 94th in Interbrand's top 100 brands.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Zurich is a [global](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transnational_company "Transnational company") insurance company which is organized into three core business segments: General Insurance, Global Life and Farmers. Zurich employs 55,000 people, with customers in 215 countries and territories.[[5]](#cite_note-5) The company is listed on [SIX Swiss Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIX_Swiss_Exchange "SIX Swiss Exchange"). As of 2012,[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit) it had a shareholders' equity of $34.494 billion.[[6]](#cite_note-ReferenceA-6)

## Company history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Company history")]

### Zurich Insurance Company (1872–1998)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Zurich Insurance Company (1872–1998)")]

The company was founded in 1872 as a [reinsurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinsurance "Reinsurance") company under the name of "Versicherungs-Verein" and at the request of the "Schweiz" transport insurance company (which was founded in 1869 on the initiative of the "Schweizerischen Kreditanstalt"), a subsidiary of the Schweiz Marine Company. It was founded by people who were also board members of the "Schweiz" transport insurance company.[[7]](#cite_note-7)

The business activity began on 1 May 1873. In 1875, [accident insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accidental_death_and_dismemberment_insurance "Accidental death and dismemberment insurance") was added. The company was renamed *Transport- und Unfall-Versicherungs-Actiengesellschaft "Zurich"*. In 1880 Zurich abandoned the marine business following a significant loss.[[8]](#cite_note-A-8)

Throughout 1894, it acquired licenses to conduct business in [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria"), [Prussia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prussia "Prussia"), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark"), [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden"), [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway"), the rest of [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France "France"), [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland"), [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg"), and [Liechtenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liechtenstein "Liechtenstein"). Due to the change in 1894 from [transport insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_insurance "Marine insurance") to accident and [liability insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liability_insurance "Liability insurance"), it was renamed "Zurich" "Allgemeine Unfall- und Haftpflicht-Versicherungs-Gesellschaft". Due to legal settlements in the area of workers' compensation, it took a risk and entered the [North American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_America "North America") market in 1912, starting in the [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"), [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois"), [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), and [Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts") in the [US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States").[[8]](#cite_note-A-8)

In 1915, Zurich acquired its first whole company, "Hispania Compañia General de Seguros" of [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona") in Spain. Ten years later, in 1922, Zurich founded "Vita Lebensversicherungs-Gesellschaft" as an independent [subsidiary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidiary "Subsidiary"), which soon expanded into neighboring countries. In addition, a branch was established in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland") (the first foreign insurance company to do so). One year later, another branch was established in [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In 1925, Zurich became the official insurer of all new [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company") vehicles in Great Britain. The "Zurich Fire Insurance Company of New York" was founded in 1929, the reinsurance company Turegum in 1938 and the "American Guarantee and Liability Company in New York" in 1939.[[8]](#cite_note-A-8)

In 1950, it bought a share in "Companhia de Seguros Metrópole S.A." of [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"). Five years later, in 1955, *«Zürich» Allgemeine Unfall- und Haftpflicht-Versicherungs-Gesellschaft* was renamed *«Zürich» Versicherungs-Gesellschaft*, a name it still holds today.[[10]](#cite_note-B-10)

Between 1955 and 1976 several companies were acquired, including the "Commonwealth General Assurance Corporation" of [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), "Iguazú Compañía de Seguros S.A." from [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires"), "Empire Fire and Marine Insurance Company" from [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska"), "Fidelity and Deposit Company" from [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland"), "Universal Underwriters" from [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), "Anglo Americana de Seguros Gerais" from [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo "São Paulo"), "Minerva Group" from [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), "Centre Reinsurance Holding" from [Bermuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bermuda "Bermuda"), "La Chilena Consolidada", and "Seguros de Vida" from [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile") and "Seguros Chapultepec" from [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico").[[8]](#cite_note-A-8)

On the initiative of "Vita Lebensversicherungs-Gesellschaft", the first Vita Parcours ([fitness trails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_trail "Fitness trail")) in Switzerland were created in 1968 and ZIM (Zurich Investment Management) was founded in 1990 as an investment management partner for [redemption funds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-end_fund "Open-end fund") and institutional investors in Switzerland. As part of a new brand strategy, "Vita" became "Zurich" Life Insurance Company in 1993, operating in the market under the name "Zürich Leben". While the name "Vita" thus disappeared from the market, it lives on in the "Stiftung Vita Parcours", which was outsourced in 1994. In 1994, "Zürich" took over the Zurich private bank "Rüd, Blass & Cie." Due to refocusing on the insurance business, the private bank was sold again in 2003.[[10]](#cite_note-B-10)

In 1996, Zurich acquired 80 percent of "Kemper Corporation" and 97 percent of "Kemper Financial Service" and in 1997 acquired a majority interest in [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City")-based "Scudder, Stevens & Clark". Subsequently, Kemper was merged with Scudder to form "Scudder Kemper Investments",[[11]](#cite_note-11) which was later renamed "Zurich Scudder Investments". Following the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks"), on 24 September 2001, Zurich Financial announced it would sell Zurich Scudder, which then had US$370 billion in [assets under management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assets_under_management "Assets under management"), to [Deutsche Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Bank "Deutsche Bank") for US$2.5 billion (US$1.2 billion in cash and the rest in assets).[[12]](#cite_note-12) The transaction was closed on 5 April 2002.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

### Zurich Financial Services (1998–2012)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Zurich Financial Services (1998–2012)")]

In September 1998, Zurich and the financial division of [British American Tobacco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_American_Tobacco "British American Tobacco") merged to form "Zurich Financial Services". This comprised the Swiss company "Zurich Allied AG",[[14]](#cite_note-14) listed on the [Swiss Market Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Market_Index "Swiss Market Index"), and the British company "Allied Zurich plc", listed on the [FTSE 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTSE_100_Index "FTSE 100 Index") ([Dual-listed Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual-listed_Company?action=edit&redlink=1 "Dual-listed Company (page does not exist)")). In 2000, the structure was reorganized under a single [holding company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holding_company "Holding company") under Swiss company law. All old shares were replaced by new shares in the newly formed "Zurich Financial Services" (ZFS) with a first [listing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Listing_(finance) "Listing (finance)") on the [SIX Swiss Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIX_Swiss_Exchange "SIX Swiss Exchange") in Zurich and a second listing in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[[15]](#cite_note-15)

In 2002, ZFS focused on insurance-related financial products and services. ZFS returned to profitability in 2003, announcing that it had met its targets and posted a profit of US$2.1 billion, compared to a loss of US$3.4 billion a year earlier. Operating income increased 93 percent to $2.3 billion, marking the turnaround. Zurich remained on track in 2004 with net income of US$2.5 billion and operating income of US$3.1 billion, an increase of 36 percent over the previous year. Zurich's net income increased by 30 percent to US$3.2 billion in 2005, and operating income rose by 32 percent to US$3.9 billion. In 2008, "Zurich Financial Services" recorded net income of US$3 billion, compared to a record US$5.7 billion in the previous year.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

In July 2011, Zurich announced that it had signed definitive agreements for a long-term alliance with "[Banco Santander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banco_Santander "Banco Santander") SA" (Santander) over 25 years in [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America").[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18)

### Zurich Insurance Group (since 2012)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Zurich Insurance Group (since 2012)")]

In April 2012, Zurich Financial Services Ltd changed back to its original name, Zurich Insurance Group Ltd. In a statement, the Group explained the rationale behind the name change. "In recognition of this strategic focus, the reference to financial services in the company name has been replaced by indicating the insurance activity of the Group instead and to specify the purpose accordingly."[[19]](#cite_note-19)

In December 2015, the CEO [Martin Senn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Senn "Martin Senn") announced his resignation. Despite years of highly profitable business operations, the focus was put on recent events which forced Senn to step down. Interim chairman [Tom de Swaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_de_Swaan?action=edit&redlink=1 "Tom de Swaan (page does not exist)") [[nl](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%20de%20Swaan "nl:Tom de Swaan")] took over as acting CEO.[[20]](#cite_note-20)

In January 2016, it was announced that Zurich had hired [Mario Greco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Greco "Mario Greco"), CEO of [Generali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assicurazioni_Generali "Assicurazioni Generali") as its next chief executive, and that he would start in May.[[21]](#cite_note-21)

Zurich Spain launched Klinc in 2018, a Spanish digital company that offers online insurance plans for cars, life, home, devices, and micromobility led by Stefano de Liguoro, Head of Digital at Zurich Seguros.[[22]](#cite_note-22) The company sprung from the multinational insurance company Zurich Seguros. In 2021, the company merged with doppo, a digital auto insurance start up. Zurich Klinc is dedicated to promoting a healthy and sustainable lifestyle. As a result, it focuses on promoting and sponsoring sporting events such as the Orbea Monegros, and the Orbea Klasika in Bilbao.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

In November 2021, Zurich signed an acquisition agreement with Texas-based Special Insurance Services.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

On 3 January 2022, Zurich Insurance Group announced that its Italian subsidiary, Zurich Investments Life S.p.A. had agreed to sell its life and pension back book to the Portuguese insurer and wealth management platform [GamaLife – Companhia de Seguros de Vida, S.A.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apax_Partners "Apax Partners") (GamaLife), for an undisclosed sum. Zurich said the transaction was expected to release approximately $1.2bn (£907m, €1bn) of capital.[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26)

In March 2022, following the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"), Zurich Insurance suspended the use of its logo containing an encircled "Z" on [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media") due to the association of [an enclosed "Z"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z_(military_symbol) "Z (military symbol)") as support of Russian violence against Ukrainians.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

In March 2026, Zurich Insurance agreed to takeover [Beazley plc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beazley_plc "Beazley plc") in a deal valued at £8.1 billion.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

## Core business segments

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Core business segments")]

### General Insurance

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: General Insurance")]

Zurich's General Insurance business serves individuals, small and medium-sized businesses and major multinational corporations with motor, home, and commercial products and services.

### Global Life

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Global Life")]

Zurich's Global Life business offers [life insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_insurance "Life insurance"),[[29]](#cite_note-29) savings, investment and pension products. In the United States life insurance is issued by Zurich American Life Insurance Company with offices in [Schaumburg, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schaumburg,_Illinois "Schaumburg, Illinois"); [Overland Park, Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overland_Park,_Kansas "Overland Park, Kansas"); and New York City.[[30]](#cite_note-30)

### Farmers

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Farmers")]

Zurich's Farmers Insurance segment includes Farmers Management Services, which provides non-claims related management services to the Farmers Exchanges (not owned by Zurich). Zurich also owns the Farmers RE business which includes reinsurance assumed from the Farmers Exchange by the Group. Zurich's [Farmers Insurance Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers_Insurance_Group "Farmers Insurance Group") is the third largest insurance group in the United States.[[31]](#cite_note-31)

### MetLife

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: MetLife")]

In December 2020, the Zurich group purchased the property and casualty insurance segment from [MetLife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetLife "MetLife") for US$3.6 billion. The purchase, combined with a 10-year cooperation agreement between Farmers and [MetLife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetLife "MetLife") is financed by Zurich group with US$2.43 billion while the remaining US$1.51 billion is contributed by Farmers.[[32]](#cite_note-32)

## Zurich Ireland

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Zurich Ireland")]

Officially known as Zurich Insurance plc ('ZIP'), Zurich Ireland is a wholly owned subsidiary. ZIP is an Irish insurance company originally incorporated in 1950 and is Zurich Insurance Group's main legal entity for writing non-life insurance business in Europe. ZIP writes non-life insurance business across the European Union through its Irish head office and network of branches.[[33]](#cite_note-33)

In July 2023, it was announced that ZIP would undergo a "cross-border conversion" from a [public limited company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_limited_company "Public limited company") in Ireland to a *[Aktiengesellschaft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aktiengesellschaft "Aktiengesellschaft")* (stock corporation) in Germany.[[34]](#cite_note-34)

## Zurich North America

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Zurich North America")]

Zurich expanded into US and Canadian market in 1912 to become one of the leading commercial [P&C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_insurance "General insurance") insurance provider. It serves a diverse set of industries including automotive, agriculture, construction, manufacturing, technology and numerous others.[[35]](#cite_note-35)

## Zurich Kotak General Insurance Company

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Zurich Kotak General Insurance Company")]

Zurich Insurance owns 70% of Zurich Kotak General Insurance in India, headquartered in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). It offers non-life insurance products like motor, car, bike, health, travel, home insurance and others.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

## Corporate social responsibility

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Corporate social responsibility")]

In 2009, Zurich was awarded [Charity Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charity_Times "Charity Times") "Best Insurance Services"[[38]](#cite_note-38) and was shortlisted again in 2010. In 2012 the Zurich Community Trust (UK) won the Cross-Sector Partnership of the Year Award for its partnership with the treatment charity Addaction.[[39]](#cite_note-39)

According to its website, Zurich Community Trust has donated over £60 million since 1972, with the goal of addressing key social issues. It has supported over 600 charities a year, making a measurable impact on the lives of over 80,000 people.[[40]](#cite_note-40) Zurich was one of the first recipients of the Community Mark from Business in the Community which it has successfully retained for three years.[[41]](#cite_note-41)

On 24 October 2002, Zurich North America hosted a ceremony at the [9/11 Tribute Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9/11_Tribute_Museum "9/11 Tribute Museum") honoring the winners of its 2012 K.A.M.P. awards, a program created as a living legacy to the four employees killed on 9/11: John Keohane, Peggy Alario, Kathy Moran and Ludwig Picarro.[[42]](#cite_note-42)

Zurich began a relationship with [SBP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SBP_(nonprofit_organization) "SBP (nonprofit organization)"), a disaster relief organization based in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"), at its Zurich Classic golf tournament in New Orleans.[[43]](#cite_note-communities-43) Over the next five years, more than 1,000 Zurich employees, customers, brokers, and distributors volunteered with SBP to rebuild homes in New Orleans, Staten Island and Joplin, until in April 2014, the company announced that its Z Zurich Foundation would give SBP a $3 million grant over three years.[[43]](#cite_note-communities-43) The grant would go towards creating a Disaster Resilience and Recovery Lab—a disaster relief model that propagates best practices learned in New Orleans after [Katrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Katrina "Hurricane Katrina") to communities affected by future disasters.[[43]](#cite_note-communities-43)

In 2011, Zurich launched a free online resource – My Community Starter – designed to make getting involved in community activities more simple.[[44]](#cite_note-44)

In March 2012, Zurich reinforced its commitment to the Z Zurich foundation by making an investment of $100 million.[[45]](#cite_note-45)

In March 2013, Zurich announced its global [flood resilience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flood_resilience "Flood resilience") program, which aims to enhance community flood resilience by finding innovative ways to increase the impact of disaster risk reduction efforts at community, national and global levels. The first country program is taking place in Mexico and Indonesia. To maximize the community impact of the program, Zurich has formed a strategic alliance with the [International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_Red_Cross_and_Red_Crescent "International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent") Societies (IFRC).[[46]](#cite_note-46)

## Controversies

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Zurich_Insurance_Group&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Controversies")]

In 2006, Zurich Financial Services settled a $171 million case relating to [bid rigging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bid_rigging "Bid rigging") and [price fixing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_fixing "Price fixing") in the United States.[[47]](#cite_note-47) "Businesses shopping for commercial insurance were deceived into believing they were getting the best deals available," said Abbott. "The whole anti-competitive scheme was an intentional smoke screen by several insurance players to artificially inflate premiums and pay improper commissions to those who brokered the deals." The states included in the settlement were Texas, California, Florida, Hawaii, Maryland, Massachusetts, Oregon, Pennsylvania and West Virginia. Zurich is also required to pay about $122 million[[48]](#cite_note-48) in refunds to commercial policyholders in a New Jersey class action lawsuit[[49]](#cite_note-49) settlement. Zurich Financial Services settled a bid-rigging and improper "finite reinsurance" transactions probe.[[50]](#cite_note-50)

Zurich Financial agreed to pay $153 million in restitution and penalties and agreed to a series of reforms. Zurich apologized and acknowledged that "certain of its employees violated both acceptable [business practices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_practice "Business practice") and Zurich's own [standards of conduct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standards_of_conduct "Standards of conduct") by engaging in improper bidding practices and the 'finite reinsurance' transactions described in the Assurance of Discontinuance". The states included in the settlement were New York, Connecticut and Illinois.[[51]](#cite_note-51)

In May 2007, Zurich Capital Markets, a subsidiary of Zurich Financial Services, paid $16.8 million to settle with the [United States Securities and Exchange Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Securities_and_Exchange_Commission "United States Securities and Exchange Commission") for helping four [hedge funds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_fund "Hedge fund") disguise their identities to avoid detection when making frequent trades in [mutual fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutual_fund "Mutual fund") shares.[[52]](#cite_note-52) An SEC director stated, "By knowingly financing their hedge funds clients' deceptive [market timing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_timing "Market timing"), ZCM reaped substantial fees at the expense of long-term mutual-fund shareholders".[[53]](#cite_note-53)

In 2015, small business owners and property developers in Britain complained that Zurich's British subsidiary, Dunbar Bank, had treated them unfairly by calling in loans quickly in order to wind down its loan book after the parent company pulled out of the specialist UK property market in 2010. They claimed that 71 Dunbar borrowers had been made bankrupt in the following five-year period, many more than by any of Britain's very much larger high street banks.[[54]](#cite_note-The_Times_30_March_2015-54) One Dunbar customer wrote: "Dunbar's latest set of accounts show that over 95% of its loan book is now classified as impaired or overdue [...] the equivalent figure for UK Asset Resolution, the country's bad bank, is just 37%".[[55]](#cite_note-Private_Eye_Issue_1392_15_May_2015-55)

In 2019, the local branch of Zurich Insurance Group was one of four insurance companies fined by Portugal's competition authority [AdC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autoridade_da_Concorrência "Autoridade da Concorrência") for "cartel practices" regarding workplace accident, health and [auto insurance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_insurance "Vehicle insurance").[[56]](#cite_note-56)

args.summary:
Zurich Insurance Group Ltd. is a Swiss insurance company headquartered in Zürich, Switzerland, founded in 1872 as a reinsurance company called "Versicherungs-Verein." It is Switzerland's largest insurer and, as of 2024, ranked 98th on Forbes' Global 2000 list. The company operates through three core business segments: General Insurance, Global Life, and Farmers. Zurich employs approximately 55,000-56,000 people and serves customers in 215 countries. It is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange under ticker ZURN.

**Company History:** The company began operations in 1873, expanded into accident insurance in 1875, and entered the North American market in 1912. It went through several name changes: Zurich Insurance Company (1872-1998), Zurich Financial Services (1998-2012), and Zurich Insurance Group (since 2012). In 1998, it merged with British American Tobacco's financial division. Key leadership includes Chairman Michel Liès and CEO Mario Greco (appointed 2016). In March 2026, Zurich agreed to acquire Beazley plc for £8.1 billion.

**Financial Performance:** Revenue: US$69.87 billion (2021). Total assets: US$435.826 billion. Total equity: US$39.170 billion.

**Key Subsidiaries:** Zurich Insurance plc (Ireland), Zurich North America (established 1912), and Zurich Kotak General Insurance in India (70% owned).

**Controversies:** In 2006, Zurich settled a $171 million bid-rigging and price-fixing case in the US. In 2007, Zurich Capital Markets paid $16.8 million to settle SEC charges for helping hedge funds disguise their identities. In 2015, Zurich's British subsidiary Dunbar Bank faced criticism for calling in loans. In 2019, Zurich was fined by Portugal's competition authority for cartel practices.

**Corporate Social Responsibility:** Zurich Community Trust has donated over £60 million since 1972. Zurich launched a global flood resilience program in 2013 in partnership with the IFRC. In 2022, Zurich suspended use of a "Z" logo on social media due to its association with Russian military symbolism during the Ukraine war.
